items.title: brigade
items.text:
Mise-en-place, ready for service.

brigade is a Copier template that adds mise tooling and CI to an existing project.

items.title: What it does
items.text:
• Pins the project's tools (linters, formatters, test runners) in .brigade/, as mise tools rather than project dependencies.
  • Defines the pipeline stages as mise tasks (mise run lint, mise run test), with the tools you pick.
  • Generates a CI that installs mise and runs those stages, for GitHub, GitLab or Gitea/Forgejo.
  • Keeps all of it up to date: mise run brigade:update applies the latest brigade release.

The same commands run on a laptop (Linux, macOS, Windows: see Platforms) and in CI.

items.title: What it does not do
items.text:
brigade sets up the kitchen; it does not cook your dish.

  • Create the project: use the ecosystem's own tool (uv init, ...), then apply brigade on top.
  • Write source code or package manifests. Tool settings are options of the mise tasks, or a file in .brigade/configs/ for tools that read one: see Tool configs.

items.title: The kitchen
items.text:
In a restaurant, the brigade is the kitchen team: each cook runs one station, the chef calls the orders, and nothing starts before the mise en place, everything prepared and in its place. mise is named after it; brigade staffs the kitchen:

In the kitchen In brigade Mise en place mise install: every tool pinned and ready before you start One station per cook One file per tool, .brigade/tools/<tool>-brigade.toml, with its tasks The service, course after course The stages: lint, build, test, release, deploy, operate The chef calling the orders mise run <stage>: every station's task for that stage The pass, where each plate is checked CI, running the same stages on every pull request The house recipe The template, with your answers in .brigade/copier/data.yml Fresh deliveries mise run brigade:update: a new release, delivered by Renovate if you like The chef inspecting the stations brigade:lint: brigade's files are as delivered, nobody salted the sauce

Next: Getting started.

items.title: CI platforms
items.text:
The pass: every plate is checked before it leaves the kitchen.

brigade generates the CI files and mise run brigade:update keeps them up to date: do not edit them. Change the stages through your answers, or add your own files.

Jobs only install mise and call mise run <stage>, so CI and laptops run the same tools.

On every platform, lint, build and test run on pull requests (merge requests on GitLab), side by side; release runs on pushes to the default branch, deploy on X.Y.Z tags and manual runs, and operate on manual runs and on the operate_schedule answer (scheduled pipelines on GitLab).

items.title: GitHub (ci: github)
items.text:
File Role .github/workflows/<stage>.yml One workflow per stage, with one job that checks out the code and runs the stage's action: lint.yml, build.yml and test.yml on pull requests, release.yml on pushes to main, deploy.yml on X.Y.Z tags and manual runs, operate.yml on manual runs and on the operate_schedule answer. .brigade/ci/github/actions/<stage>/action.yml The stage's steps: install mise and the tools, then mise run <stage> with the stage's environment (Releasaurus, Renovate). Secrets are passed as inputs: token (release), renovate-token (operate). .brigade/ci/github/actions/mise/action.yml Installs the pinned mise (mise-action) and the tools, with a cache. deploy installs them without a cache.

GitHub only reads workflows in .github/workflows/: everything else lives in .brigade/.

jactionlint (jactionlint:lint) checks the workflows and the actions, with its default rules: actions pinned by commit SHA (Renovate updates the SHA and its version comment), permissions:, timeout-minutes, concurrency: (pull request runs cancel the older ones, release and deploy runs wait), and no cache restored in deploy.

items.title: Stages
items.text: Each stage is one workflow with one job, on Linux, running its action. To remove a stage or change its commands, see Stages.

items.title: Your own jobs
items.text:
For anything else (several OSes, other triggers), add your own workflow file next to them, with another name: brigade never touches it.

# .github/workflows/tests-os.yml
on:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
      - uses: ./.brigade/ci/github/actions/test

items.title: GitLab (ci: gitlab)
items.text:
File Role .gitlab-ci.yml Stages, and includes every .brigade/ci/gitlab/*.yml and .gitlab/ci/*.yml. GitLab only reads this file. .brigade/ci/gitlab/default.yml The mise image, the tool cache and mise install. .brigade/ci/gitlab/<stage>.yml One job per stage, running mise run <stage>: lint, build and test in merge request pipelines (needs: [], side by side), release on pushes to the default branch, deploy on X.Y.Z tags and "Run pipeline", operate in scheduled pipelines.

To add jobs, create your own file in .gitlab/ci/: it is included automatically, and GitLab merges included files.

# .gitlab/ci/extra.yml
extra:
  stage: test
  script:
    - mise run lint

gitlab-ci:lint checks these files against the GitLab CI schema.

items.title: Manual run
items.text: To deploy without a release, use "Run workflow" on the Deploy workflow (GitHub, Gitea), or "Run pipeline" on GitLab: only deploy runs. To run operate now, use "Run workflow" on the Operate workflow (GitHub, Gitea), or a pipeline schedule on GitLab.

items.title: Gitea and Forgejo (ci: gitea)
items.text:
Same layout as GitHub: .gitea/workflows/<stage>.yml and .brigade/ci/gitea/actions/.

  • mise is installed with its install script: Forgejo resolves actions from its own mirror, which has actions/checkout but not mise-action, and act (local runs) refuses full URLs. The script checks the archive against a checksum file from the same server, so it trusts HTTPS only: jactionlint:lint ignores that one finding (unverified-download).

items.title: None (ci: none)
items.text: Only .miserc.toml and .brigade/ (without ci/) are generated.

items.title: Contributing
items.text: Back of house: something burned, a tool missing from the station, or a hand in the kitchen.

items.title: Issues
items.text:
Open an issue with one of the forms:

  • 🔥 Something burned: a task, a generated file or the CI does not work as documented. Give your brigade version (_commit in .brigade/copier/answers.yml), the command and its full output, and your .brigade/copier/data.yml: with it, the same project can be generated to reproduce the bug. Try mise run brigade:update first: it may already be fixed.
  • 🔪 New tool for the station: a tool for the catalog. It must install with mise and run on its own; tools already planned are listed in #138.
  • 🧑‍🍳 New recipe: any other idea. Start with the need, then the idea.

Search the existing issues first, and never paste a secret or token.

items.title: Development
items.text:
Working on brigade itself. Requires mise and a running Docker (the variants replay their CI with act and gitlab-ci-local).

mise install
mise run brigade:hooks    # optional: lint before each commit
mise run lint
mise run build            # the documentation site, strict
mise run test
mise run zensical:serve   # preview the site

items.title: Repository
items.text:
• copier.yml includes .copier/settings.yml and .copier/questions/: common.yml, then one file per tool in tools/.
  • template/ holds the generated files.
  • ctt.toml lists the test variants.
  • docs/ and zensical.toml hold this site.

brigade is generated by brigade: .miserc.toml, .brigade/ and the .github/workflows/ files come from the latest release, with the answers in .brigade/copier/data.yml (taplo's file list, ctt:test clearing .ctt/ first, the Renovate config path), and the lint settings skipping template/ and .ctt/ in .brigade/configs/. mise run brigade:update updates them after a release. brigade's own settings (the .ctt/ env) live in mise.toml: brigade is tested with the tools it ships, nothing written by hand.

items.title: Lint
items.text: mise run lint checks this repo: yamllint, jactionlint, zizmor (brigade's own workflows and actions), taplo, editorconfig-checker, gitleaks, typos, ruff and ty (the scripts), rumdl (Markdown), lychee (links, external ones included: it needs the network), ls-lint (names) and the Renovate config schema.

items.title: Tests
items.text:
mise run test runs ctt:test: ctt renders each ctt.toml variant into .ctt/, creates a real project there with the ecosystem's tool, then runs its stages. Their test stage includes act:test or gitlab-ci-local:test, which replay each generated CI in Docker. ctt only sees files tracked by git: git add new template files before testing.

brigade's CI runs these tests on Linux only.

mise run build builds this site in strict mode, which fails on broken links. CI deploys it (pages:deploy, to the gh-pages branch) on each release tag and on a manual run of the Deploy workflow.

items.title: Versions and releases
items.text:
Pinned versions are updated by Renovate (.github/renovate.json5), run every Monday by the generated Operate workflow (mise run operate, operate_schedule) as one PR, fix(deps): update template, major updates included: it triggers a release.

Renovate only reads template/. brigade's generated files get the new versions like any project, through a release and mise run brigade:update; its other pins (Copier and pytest in ctt.toml, README.md and .copier/settings.yml) are updated by hand.

It needs a RENOVATE_TOKEN secret: a fine-grained token on this repo with contents, pull requests, issues, workflows and commit statuses read/write.

Commits and PR titles follow Conventional Commits. On each push to main, the CI's release job runs Releasaurus (mise run release): it opens or updates the release PR, and once merged tags X.Y.Z and updates CHANGELOG.md; Copier uses these tags as template versions. releasaurus.toml makes a release on feat, fix, perf, revert and breaking changes only: other commits do not change the template.

It uses the RELEASAURUS_GITHUB_TOKEN secret, a fine-grained token on this repo with contents, issues and pull requests read/write: unlike the workflow token, its release PR runs the checks and its tag starts the Deploy workflow.

items.title: Custom tasks
items.text:
The chef's specials: your own tasks, next to the house menu.

mise reads the files listed in .miserc.toml: brigade's, in .brigade/, then your own mise.toml and mise.local.toml at the project root. Copier never touches them, so your tasks and tools survive brigade:update. A file elsewhere (such as .mise/conf.d/) is not read.

A task named <name>:<stage> joins that stage, because each stage runs *:<stage>:

# mise.toml
[tools]
hadolint = "2.15.1"

[tasks."hadolint:lint"]
description = "Check the Dockerfile with hadolint"
run = "hadolint Dockerfile"

[tasks."integration:test"]
description = "Run integration tests"
run = "uv run pytest tests/integration"

mise run lint and mise run test now include them, locally and in CI.

items.title: Getting started
items.text:
Tie your apron: your first service starts here.

Requires mise and git.

items.title: Create the project, then apply brigade
items.text:
uv init my-project
uvx copier@9.19.1 copy gh:pa-decarvalho/brigade my-project
cd my-project
mise install
mise tasks

Copier asks a few questions: your tools, whether to customize their versions and commands, CI platform, optional mirrors. copier copy uses the latest release; add --vcs-ref X.Y.Z to pick a version.

items.title: Run the stages
items.text:
mise run lint
mise run test

items.title: Lint before each commit
items.text:
mise run brigade:hooks

This writes a git hook in .git/hooks/ that runs mise run brigade:pre-commit. The task is defined by brigade, so brigade:update keeps it up to date.

items.title: Generated files
items.text:
.miserc.toml                      # the mise files to read: brigade's, then your mise.toml
.brigade/
  copier/answers.yml              # your answers, written by Copier
  copier/data.yml                 # your answers, to edit: applied by brigade:update
  configs/                        # your tool configs, created once (yamllint.yml, ruff.toml...)
  mise.toml                       # uv and brigade:update
  stages.toml                     # the stages and the git hook tasks
  mirror.toml                     # only with mirrors
  tools/<tool>-brigade.toml       # one per tool, e.g. ruff-brigade.toml, and the CI file linter
  ci/<ci>/                        # CI steps: actions (GitHub, Gitea), jobs (GitLab)
<CI files>                        # workflows or .gitlab-ci.yml: see CI platforms

Your own tasks and tools go in mise.toml: see Custom tasks.

items.title: Mirrors
items.text:
Your own suppliers, for kitchens that cannot shop at the open market.

Behind a corporate network, optional questions point downloads at internal mirrors (e.g. Nexus). They are written to .brigade/mirror.toml; leave them empty to download from the internet.

Question Example Used for github_mirror https://nexus.example.com/repository/github/ Tools mise downloads from GitHub releases (mise url_replacements). pypi_index https://nexus.example.com/repository/pypi/simple Python tools installed by mise (pipx:), and uv / uvx in tasks (UV_DEFAULT_INDEX).

mise still reads release metadata from mise-versions.jdx.dev or api.github.com. Allow them, or see mise's URL replacements.

items.title: Questions
items.text:
Taking the order: what goes on the menu.

Answers are saved in .brigade/copier/data.yml, where you change them (see Changing answers), and in .brigade/copier/answers.yml, Copier's own copy (do not edit).

Question Values Default Effect presets python, go, terraform, ansible, shell, docker, lua, docs, copier-template, security, ci, maintenance (each answered as its tool list) none Pre-select their tools in tools: see Presets. tools tools of the catalog brigade, yamllint, gitleaks, typos One .brigade/tools/<tool>-brigade.toml each, with its tasks. Stages follow from the tools. <stage>_enabled yes / no yes Keeps the stage: its mise task and its CI job. See Stages. <stage>_commands list of commands empty Commands of the stage, run in order, locally and in CI. Empty runs all its tools. operate_schedule cron expression, e.g. 0 5 * * 1 empty GitHub, Gitea: when the Operate workflow runs, besides manual runs. Empty: manual runs only. On GitLab, set a pipeline schedule instead. customize_tools yes / no no Asks a version and a command for each selected tool: see Tools. ci github, gitlab, gitea, none github CI files and their linter: see CI platforms. github_mirror URL empty Mirror of https://github.com/: see Mirrors. pypi_index URL empty PyPI simple index: see Mirrors.

items.title: Changing answers
items.text:
Your answers are all in .brigade/copier/data.yml. Edit them there, then run mise run brigade:update:

# Your answers: edit them, then run mise run brigade:update.
build_commands:
  - "uv build"
ci: "gitlab"
customize_tools: true
ruff_version: "0.16.0"
tools:
  - "brigade"
  - "ruff"

brigade:update applies them, then writes all the answers back to this file, sorted, with JSON values (double quotes) and lists indented under their key:

  • New questions of a release show up with their default (Renovate's update PR included): change them there too.
  • A removed key comes back with its last value: set the value you want instead.
  • A key that is not a question (a typo), or a question not asked (tool versions need customize_tools: true), is dropped.
  • Your comments and formatting are not kept.

When data.yml is your only change, brigade:update applies it without a commit first: review and commit the edit and the update together. Your edits are kept if the update fails or is stopped; after a killed run, the next brigade:update puts them back first (they wait in .git/brigade-data.yml). With other uncommitted changes, Copier refuses to update: commit them first. Until you run brigade:update, brigade:lint fails: the answers are not applied yet.

items.title: Tools
items.text:
The stations of the brigade, and who works at each one.

Pick your tools in one list when applying brigade. A tool brings its version and all its tasks, in one file: .brigade/tools/<tool>-brigade.toml, listed in .miserc.toml. Its tasks run at the project root.

Tasks are named <tool>:<action>. Stages run in this order: lint, build, test, release, deploy, operate, and each runs every <tool>:<stage> task. Any other action, such as zensical:serve, stays out of the pipeline.

items.title: Stages
items.text:
For each stage, Copier asks whether to keep it, then its commands.

  • Answer no to remove the stage: no mise task, no CI job.
  • Leave the commands empty to run all the stage's tools. A stage without tools does nothing.
  • Give commands to run them instead, in order, locally and in CI:
lint_commands: ["mise run ruff:lint", "mise run typos:lint"]

items.title: Presets
items.text:
The presets question, asked before tools, pre-selects tools: tick or untick them in tools before going on. Only tools decides what the project gets; a preset changed in a later brigade release does not change existing projects. A preset's answer is its tool list, e.g. presets: [[ruff, ty, pytest, uv]] in .brigade/copier/data.yml.

Preset Tools python ruff, ty, pytest, uv go golangci-lint terraform tflint, checkov, opentofu ansible ansible-lint, molecule, ansible shell shellcheck, shfmt docker hadolint lua stylua docs rumdl, zensical, pages (GitHub, GitLab) copier-template ctt security osv-scanner, checkov, zizmor (GitHub) ci act (GitHub, Gitea) or gitlab-ci-local (GitLab): replays the CI maintenance renovate, releasaurus

items.title: Catalog
items.text:
brigade, yamllint, gitleaks and typos are selected by default.

Tool Task Command brigade brigade:lint Fails when a brigade-owned file was edited or deleted: see brigade yamllint yamllint:lint yamllint --strict (config) gitleaks gitleaks:lint gitleaks git (history and staged changes) typos typos:lint typos (config) editorconfig-checker editorconfig-checker:lint editorconfig-checker (needs your .editorconfig; config) taplo taplo:lint taplo fmt --check on .brigade/**/*.toml and .miserc.toml (config) renovate renovate:lint check-jsonschema --builtin-schema vendor.renovate renovate.json (other config path: change the command) renovate:operate renovate (needs RENOVATE_TOKEN and RENOVATE_REPOSITORIES: see operate); also opens a PR updating brigade on each release ruff ruff:lint ruff check && ruff format --check (config) ty ty:lint uv sync && ty check (uv sync: ty reads the project's .venv; config) shellcheck shellcheck:lint shellcheck on every *.sh and *.bash (outside hidden folders); none: nothing to check shfmt shfmt:lint shfmt --diff on the same files (style: your .editorconfig) rumdl rumdl:lint rumdl check --no-cache . (Markdown; config) markdownlint markdownlint:lint markdownlint-cli2 "**/*.md", without .mise-data/, .venv/ and node_modules/; reads your .markdownlint-cli2.* or .markdownlint.*. Same rules as rumdl: pick one vale vale:lint vale sync && vale . (prose in Markdown, with Vale's built-in style), without .mise-data/, .venv/ and node_modules/ (config; vale sync downloads the style packages it lists) lychee lychee:lint lychee --no-progress . (links in Markdown, HTML and text files, outside hidden folders and CHANGELOG.md, whose release PR links to a tag not made yet); reads your lychee.toml. Checks external links: a dead link fails an unchanged project codespell codespell:lint codespell, outside hidden folders (config) cspell cspell:lint cspell lint ., outside hidden folders (config). Checks every word against its dictionaries, unlike typos and codespell: add your project's words to the config's words, listed by mise exec -- cspell lint --words-only --unique . ls-lint ls-lint:lint ls-lint: file and folder names (config: set your naming rules, none until then) sqlfluff sqlfluff:lint sqlfluff lint on every *.sql (outside hidden folders); none: nothing to check (config: set your SQL dialect) prettier prettier:lint prettier --check . (JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON, YAML, Markdown, CSS...), without .mise-data/, .venv/ and .brigade/; reads your .prettierrc and .prettierignore biome biome:lint biome ci . (JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON, CSS, Markdown: lint and formatting), without what git ignores, .mise-data/, .venv/ and .brigade/ (config). Formats the same files as prettier: pick one clang-format clang-format:lint clang-format --dry-run --Werror on every C and C++ file (outside hidden folders), with your .clang-format (else LLVM style); none: nothing to check trivy trivy:lint trivy fs .: vulnerable dependencies and secrets (config); downloads its vulnerability database, so a new vulnerability can fail an unchanged project osv-scanner osv-scanner:lint osv-scanner scan source --recursive on your lockfiles (uv.lock, package-lock.json...), without .mise-data/; queries osv.dev, so a new vulnerability can fail an unchanged project golangci-lint golangci-lint:lint golangci-lint run (needs Go: pin go in your mise.toml) revive revive:lint revive -set_exit_status ./... (Go, golint's rules; faster than golangci-lint, which can run revive too), outside hidden folders; -config revive.toml in your command for your rules tflint tflint:lint tflint --recursive (Terraform) opentofu opentofu:lint tofu fmt -check -recursive (Terraform and OpenTofu formatting), outside hidden folders checkov checkov:lint checkov on the project (Terraform, Kubernetes, Dockerfiles, workflows...), with no download from Prisma Cloud and without reading the repository's settings through the GitHub API (config) cfn-lint cfn-lint:lint cfn-lint on every YAML or JSON file holding AWSTemplateFormatVersion (CloudFormation and SAM templates, outside hidden folders); none: nothing to check dotenv-linter dotenv-linter:lint dotenv-linter check --recursive . (.env files), without .mise-data/ stylua stylua:lint stylua --check . (Lua) ansible-lint ansible-lint:lint ansible-lint --strict (config) hadolint hadolint:lint hadolint on every *Dockerfile* and *Containerfile* (outside hidden folders); none: nothing to check zizmor zizmor:lint GitHub: zizmor --offline . audits the workflows and actions for security issues. brigade's own files pass; their # zizmor: ignore[...] comments keep ./ for local actions (act has no $/ syntax) and allow fixed values written to GITHUB_ENV uv uv:build uv build (into dist/) zensical zensical:build zensical build --strict (needs your zensical.toml and docs/: zensical new .) zensical:serve zensical serve --open, to preview the site pytest pytest:test uv run pytest (add it with uv add --dev pytest) molecule molecule:test molecule test --all, with the Docker driver (needs your molecule/<scenario>/molecule.yml and Docker: see Molecule) molecule:converge, molecule:verify, molecule:destroy molecule converge, verify, destroy, while writing a role molecule:reconverge molecule:destroy, then molecule converge, to converge from scratch molecule:login molecule login, a shell in the instance ctt ctt:test ctt, for a Copier template (needs your ctt.toml) releasaurus releasaurus:release releasaurus release && releasaurus release-pr --tag-prefix '': see release pages pages:deploy Runs the *:build tasks, then publishes site/. GitHub: ghp-import -n -p -f site. GitLab: the job publishes it ansible ansible:deploy, ansible:operate ansible-playbook -i inventory playbooks/deploy.yml (operate.yml): see Ansible act act:test GitHub, Gitea: act pull_request replays the pull request workflows in Docker: see below gitlab-ci-local gitlab-ci-local:test GitLab: gitlab-ci-local replays the merge request pipeline in Docker: see below

The CI platform adds its own linter (jactionlint:lint, gitlab-ci:lint): see CI platforms.

items.title: Tool configs
items.text:
Tools that read a config file get one in .brigade/configs/, created with brigade's settings when the tool is selected (the folders to skip, such as .mise-data/, the GitLab CI tool cache). The file is yours: edit it, brigade never changes it again (brigade:update keeps it, brigade:lint skips it). Removing the tool from tools removes it. Paths in it are relative to the project root.

Tool Config Your usual config file yamllint .brigade/configs/yamllint.yml .yamllint: not read ruff .brigade/configs/ruff.toml [tool.ruff] in pyproject.toml, ruff.toml: not read ty .brigade/configs/ty.toml [tool.ty] in pyproject.toml, ty.toml: not read typos .brigade/configs/typos.toml _typos.toml, typos.toml: still read, both apply taplo .brigade/configs/taplo.toml taplo.toml: not read rumdl .brigade/configs/rumdl.toml .rumdl.toml: not read editorconfig-checker .brigade/configs/editorconfig-checker.json .editorconfig-checker.json: not read (.editorconfig still is) ansible-lint .brigade/configs/ansible-lint.yml .ansible-lint: not read vale .brigade/configs/vale.ini .vale.ini: not read codespell .brigade/configs/codespell.cfg .codespellrc: not read biome .brigade/configs/biome-brigade.jsonc biome.json, biome.jsonc: not read trivy .brigade/configs/trivy.yaml trivy.yaml: not read sqlfluff .brigade/configs/sqlfluff.cfg .sqlfluff: still read, the brigade file wins (its dialect) checkov .brigade/configs/checkov.yml .checkov.yaml: not read cspell .brigade/configs/cspell.yaml cspell.json, .cspell.json...: still read, both apply ls-lint .brigade/configs/ls-lint.yml .ls-lint.yml: not read

Move your settings into the brigade file. Other tools read their usual config file (.golangci.yml, .tflint.hcl, stylua.toml, lychee.toml, .markdownlint-cli2.yaml, .prettierrc, .clang-format...).

Before brigade 0.15, these settings were command-line options: brigade:update creates the files with the same settings. A file brigade creates is not updated by later releases: compare it with the template when a release changes it (release notes).

items.title: Platforms
items.text:
brigade's own files run on Linux, macOS and Windows; each tool runs where it is supported. CI runs on Linux, so these limits only matter for local runs (mise run <stage>, git hooks). Known limits on Windows:

  • taplo: fails on checkouts with CRLF line endings (git config core.autocrlf false, or * text eol=lf in .gitattributes).
  • ctt: ctt 3.0.0 fails inside a git repository.
  • ansible-lint, molecule, ansible: Ansible does not run on Windows (use WSL).
  • act, gitlab-ci-local: need Docker with Linux containers (Docker Desktop, WSL 2).

items.title: brigade
items.text:
brigade:lint renders the template at the version of .brigade/copier/answers.yml, with your answers, into a temporary folder, and compares it with your brigade-owned files (.miserc.toml, .brigade/, the generated workflows or .gitlab-ci.yml). An edited or deleted file fails the lint stage, locally, in the git hook and in CI: brigade:update would overwrite it. Run mise run brigade:update to restore them. An edited .brigade/copier/data.yml fails it too until brigade:update applies it (see Changing answers).

It also tells when a newer brigade release is out (copier check-update), without failing: run mise run brigade:update, or let Renovate open the PR.

It needs access to the template (gh:pa-decarvalho/brigade, through git) on each run. Offline, behind a proxy, or to edit a generated file on purpose, remove brigade from your tools.

items.title: release
items.text:
CI runs this stage on its own, on pushes to the default branch (main): lint, build and test already ran on the pull request.

With releasaurus, Releasaurus reads the Conventional Commits since the last tag and opens or updates a release pull request, with the next version and a CHANGELOG.md. Once you merge it, the next run tags X.Y.Z (no v) and publishes the release on your forge. It works on GitHub, GitLab, Gitea and Forgejo.

By default, every Conventional Commit (ci:, docs:, chore:...) makes a release. To release on feat and fix only, add a releasaurus.toml that skips the other groups, which also leaves them out of CHANGELOG.md:

[defaults.versioning.named_parsers]
refactor.skip = true
documentation.skip = true
style.skip = true
test.skip = true
chore.skip = true
ci.skip = true
miscellaneous.skip = true

See Releasaurus commit groups.

On GitHub and Gitea, it works with the CI's own token, but the release pull request and the tag it makes start no CI: merge the release pull request with a bypass of the required checks, and run deploy by hand. With a bot token, both start the CI as usual. GitLab needs the token.

CI Secret or CI/CD variable (bot token) Scopes GitHub RELEASAURUS_GITHUB_TOKEN Contents, Issues and Pull requests: read and write GitLab RELEASAURUS_GITLAB_TOKEN api, write_repository Gitea, Forgejo RELEASAURUS_GITEA_TOKEN repository, issue and misc: read and write

items.title: deploy
items.text:
CI runs this stage on its own, on tags X.Y.Z (or vX.Y.Z), such as the ones Releasaurus pushes, and on a manual run, to deploy without a release: for example to fix a typo in the documentation.

pages needs GitHub or GitLab, and a <tool>:build task that writes site/: zensical, or your own (for example mkdocs:build, see Custom tasks).

  • GitHub: the site is pushed to the gh-pages branch. In Settings → Pages, choose "Deploy from a branch" and gh-pages.
  • GitLab: the job publishes site/ with pages.publish (GitLab 17.10 or later).

Add site/ and .cache/ to your .gitignore.

items.title: operate
items.text:
Operations that do not belong to a release, such as renovate:operate. Run it with mise run operate, or in CI:

  • GitHub, Gitea: "Run workflow" on the Operate workflow, and on the operate_schedule answer (a cron expression, e.g. 0 5 * * 1 for Mondays at 5:00 UTC).
  • GitLab: scheduled pipelines only (CI/CD → Schedules; "Play" runs one now), since "Run pipeline" deploys.

For Renovate, CI sets the platform, the endpoint and the repository; add a RENOVATE_TOKEN secret (CI/CD variable on GitLab). On GitHub, the job commits as the token's owner, with their noreply address (RENOVATE_GIT_AUTHOR); elsewhere, set gitAuthor in your Renovate config if needed. See Renovate's token permissions.

items.title: brigade updates
items.text:
renovate:operate also follows brigade: on a new release, it opens a PR that runs mise run brigade:update to that version, on every CI platform. Copier shows conflicts with your edits as inline markers in the PR: fix them there before merging (brigade:lint fails until then). On GitHub, the token also needs the Workflows permission, since updates change workflow files.

Renovate reads this from its global config (RENOVATE_CONFIG, set by the task): your Renovate config can still change the PR, for example its commit type with a packageRules entry on matchDepNames: ["brigade"]. If it sets includePaths, add .brigade/copier/answers.yml. Keep brigade out of groups (such as group:all): Copier needs a clean tree, so the update must be its own PR.

To update every day and merge automatically once the checks pass, answer operate_schedule: "0 5 * * *", add automerge: true to your Renovate config and make your checks required (GitHub: a branch ruleset, and "Allow auto-merge" in Settings). A failing check, or Copier's conflict markers in a brigade update, keep the PR open.

items.title: Ansible
items.text:
ansible installs ansible-core and runs your playbooks on your inventory: playbooks/deploy.yml in the deploy stage (on X.Y.Z tags and manual runs), playbooks/operate.yml in the operate stage (manual runs and operate_schedule), both with -i inventory. Other paths or options: change the commands (ansible_deploy_command, ansible_operate_command), or add ansible.cfg.

In CI, two optional secrets (CI/CD variables on GitLab, of type Variable):

  • ANSIBLE_PRIVATE_KEY: the SSH private key. Ansible loads it into an SSH agent of its own (ANSIBLE_SSH_AGENT=auto, ansible-core 2.19 or later), with no key file. Without it, the tasks keep your own SSH setup. On GitLab, brigade's image has no SSH client yet (#139).
  • ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD: the vault password. When it is set, the tasks add --vault-password-file .brigade/scripts/ansible-vault-password.py, a script that prints it. Without it, Ansible uses your own setup (ansible.cfg, ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE), so it works the same locally: ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD=... mise run deploy.

Lint the playbooks with ansible-lint, test roles with molecule.

items.title: Toolchain
items.text: Create the project with uv init: uv is always installed, and picks Python from .python-version and requires-python.

items.title: Molecule
items.text:
molecule:test runs every scenario of molecule/ (molecule test --all), with the Docker driver of molecule-plugins and ansible-core installed alongside. molecule init scenario writes a scenario to fill in; for Docker, set the driver and an image with Python (pre_build_image uses it as is; without it, the driver builds an image and needs rsync):

# molecule/default/molecule.yml
driver:
  name: docker
platforms:
  - name: instance
    image: docker.io/library/python:3.13-slim
    pre_build_image: true

The other tasks stay out of the pipeline and work on the default scenario. Arguments go to the command: mise run molecule:converge -- -s <scenario>; molecule:reconverge passes them to converge only (its molecule:destroy takes the default scenario). The tasks run Molecule with mise exec pipx:molecule@<version>, so that its ansible-playbook (with the Docker libraries) comes before the ansible tool's.

It needs Docker, also in CI: GitHub runners and act have it; on GitLab and Gitea, the runner must give the job access to a Docker daemon (mounted socket or DOCKER_HOST).

items.title: Run the CI locally
items.text:
Pick act (GitHub, Gitea) or gitlab-ci-local (GitLab): act:test or gitlab-ci-local:test replays the CI of pull requests in Docker, as part of the test stage.

  • It needs Docker, also in CI: GitHub runners have it; on GitLab, the task does nothing in a pipeline, and on Gitea it depends on the runner.
  • Inside the replayed CI, its test job runs the task again: there it does nothing (act sets ACT, gitlab-ci-local sets GITLAB_CI), so the replay does not loop.
  • In CI, the test job then replays the whole CI once more, which takes longer.

items.title: Customize a version or a command
items.text:
Each tool has one file with its version and its commands. Answer yes to customize_tools and Copier asks, for each selected tool, a version and a command:

Customize tool versions and commands? (y/N) y
ruff version (empty for brigade's):
Command of ruff:lint (empty for brigade's): ruff check src
  • An answer replaces brigade's value, and stays on brigade:update until you change it.
  • An empty answer takes brigade's value, and keeps following it on brigade:update. Clear an answer to go back to it.

Answers are named <tool>_version and <tool>_<action>_command, e.g. ruff_version, zensical_serve_command. To change them later, see Questions.

Missing a tool? Add your own task: see Custom tasks.

items.title: Updating
items.text:
Fresh deliveries: a new brigade release, straight to your kitchen.

mise run brigade:update

This runs copier update with the answers in .brigade/copier/answers.yml (edited in .brigade/copier/data.yml, see Changing answers) and applies the latest brigade release: new tool versions, new tasks, CI changes. Commit your work first: Copier needs a clean git tree, and shows conflicts as inline markers.

With the renovate tool, Renovate opens this update as a PR on each release (see brigade updates); with the brigade tool, brigade:lint tells when a release is out.

brigade releases are tagged X.Y.Z. Tool versions are bumped by Renovate in brigade, so a project gets them through a release and brigade:update.

items.title: What is overwritten
items.text:
Files generated by brigade belong to brigade: local edits show up as conflicts on update. The brigade tool (brigade:lint) catches them before: see brigade.

Files you add are yours: brigade never touches them, such as mise.toml, your own workflows or .gitlab/ci/*.yml files.

See CI platforms. For your own tasks, see Custom tasks.

items.title: From brigade 0.12 and earlier
items.text:
Since 0.13, the answers are in .brigade/copier/. Update as usual (or merge Renovate's PR), then move them:

mise run brigade:update
git mv .brigade/answers.yml .brigade/copier/answers.yml
git commit -m "chore: move brigade answers"

Until then, brigade:lint fails and brigade:update cannot find the answers.

items.title: From brigade 0.5 and earlier
items.text:
Before 0.6, brigade's files were in .mise/ and .github/actions/ (.gitea/actions/, .gitlab/ci/). Move your answers, then update:

mkdir -p .brigade/copier
git mv .mise/brigade-copier-answers.yml .brigade/copier/answers.yml
git commit -m "chore: move brigade answers"
uvx copier@9.19.1 update -a .brigade/copier/answers.yml

Copier removes the old generated files. Move your own files out of .mise/ into mise.toml (see Custom tasks): mise no longer reads .mise/.
